question: What is the main goal of having a menu in a hospital or clinic kitchen?

options.A: To list food and drink items to meet nutritional and financial needs
options.B: To calculate the daily profit margin of the hospital kitchen
options.C: To dictate the cleaning schedule for the food preparation staff
options.D: To provide a strict legal record of patient drug administration

explanation: A menu is simply a guide to make sure meals meet nutritional, cultural, and budget needs!

question: Why should as a nurse you care about hospital menu planning?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for clinical dietitians in the ward
options.B: To help coordinate dietary needs and ensure patients eat therapeutic diets
options.C: To independently price food items for patient billing accounts
options.D: To take over the daily cooking duties of the hospital kitchen staff

explanation: You work hand-in-hand with the dietary team to make sure your patients actually get the healing nutrition prescribed for them.

question: Which of these is a common local carbohydrate staple you will see in Nigerian menu planning?
explanation: Garri, made from cassava, is a widely enjoyed and accessible energy source right here at home!

question: Why must hospital menus in Nigeria include familiar local food staples?

options.A: To strictly reduce the total daily calorie count for every patient
options.B: To comply with international import regulations from foreign countries
options.C: To completely replace the need for dietary proteins in hospital diets
options.D: To ensure meals are culturally acceptable and familiar to the consumers

explanation: When patients see familiar, tasty local dishes, they are much happier to eat and recover faster.

question: What is a major plus when you use seasonal food ingredients for a menu?

options.A: It guarantees that all meals will be completely fat-free
options.B: It removes all cultural restrictions from the meal plan
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for food preservation
options.D: It lowers food costs and guarantees ingredient freshness

explanation: In-season foods are harvested locally in plenty, making them cheaper and way fresher for the kitchen.

question: A hospital kitchen is planning meals for patients who do not eat pork due to religious beliefs. What is guiding this menu choice?
explanation: Respecting religious and cultural food laws is a vital part of caring for the whole patient.

question: What do you call a menu that repeats itself after a set time, like every two weeks?
explanation: A cycle menu rotates through a set list of days, which is a lifesaver for busy hospitals and schools.

question: Why do hospitals love using cycle menus?

options.A: They provide variety while simplifying food purchasing and kitchen planning
options.B: They ensure that all meals are served at zero financial cost
options.C: They guarantee that every patient eats the exact same food forever
options.D: They allow the kitchen to completely avoid checking food expiration dates

explanation: Cycle menus keep patients from getting bored with food while helping the kitchen budget and buy supplies easily.

question: When designing a daily meal, which part should you usually plan first?

options.A: Main dishes like proteins and primary starches

explanation: The proteins and starches are the heavy lifters of the meal; you build the rest around them!

question: Why is it smart to check a menu for a nice mix of colors, textures, and flavors?

options.A: It guarantees that the food will require zero cooking preparation time
options.B: It stimulates appetite and makes the meal more enjoyable to eat
options.C: It prevents the kitchen staff from having to wash dishes afterwards
options.D: It ensures that every food item tastes exactly the same

explanation: Nobody wants a boring, pale plate! Colorful, well-textured food makes patients actually want to eat.

question: What is a great way institutional kitchens keep food costs under control?

options.A: Serving only imported luxury foods every single day
options.B: Eliminating all vegetables from the daily meal plan
options.C: Ignoring food waste and throwing away leftover ingredients
options.D: Practicing careful portion control and buying in bulk

explanation: Buying in large quantities and serving the right portions helps save money and cuts down waste.

question: How does menu planning directly impact the budget of a food service unit?

options.A: It has no impact whatsoever on the overall kitchen expenses
options.B: It automatically sets the electricity tariff for the entire hospital building
options.C: It dictates the monthly salary of all administrative personnel
options.D: It determines the types of ingredients purchased and the amount of waste generated

explanation: The menu dictates your shopping list, which directly controls how much money you spend and waste.

question: What does a lot of leftover food ('plate waste') usually tell you about a meal?

options.A: That the kitchen budget is currently running a surplus
options.B: That the patients are eating far too much food
options.C: That the menu has too many different color varieties
options.D: A problem with food taste, texture, or acceptance

explanation: If food keeps coming back untouched, it usually means the patients aren't enjoying how it tastes or looks.

question: What does evaluating a menu mean in quality improvement?

options.A: A strict punishment system for kitchen staff who make cooking errors
options.B: A continuous process of gathering feedback and adjusting meals to meet client needs
options.C: A one-time inspection that happens only when the kitchen first opens
options.D: A method to permanently stop changing the food served in the ward

explanation: It's all about checking in regularly, listening to patient feedback, and tweaking the menu so everyone is well-fed and happy.
